base_changes.content: Supplier portal stock exports (e.g. exports/stock-2026-10-27.csv) start with a UTF-8 BOM, so restock.py with its default --encoding utf-8 fails with "column 'sku' not found ... header is ['﻿sku', ...]". Workaround without editing the export or script: python3 restock.py --encoding utf-8-sig exports/<file>.csv

record.final_answer:
These 4 SKUs need reordering, based on exports/stock-2026-10-27.csv:

| SKU | Stock (all warehouses) | Reorder level |
|---|---|---|
| BX-100 | 23 | 25 |
| CL-310 | 5 | 5 |
| EN-512 | 0 | 10 |
| GH-118 | 7 | 12 |

BX-220, DR-045 and FT-760 have enough stock.

The plain run, `python3 restock.py exports/stock-2026-10-27.csv`, fails with "column 'sku' not found". The export starts with a hidden byte-order mark (a few invisible bytes at the very start of the file), so the script reads the first column name as `\ufeffsku` instead of `sku`. Running with `--encoding utf-8-sig`, an option the script already has, gets past it. I didn't change the export or restock.py.

I saved this in memcue (the long-term memory) so later sessions run it the same way.
